ca_western_wall_the.blurb: The Western Wall is one of roughly ten crags that make up the Western Wall Area in the Alabama Hills outside Lone Pine. It has nine routes: seven sport and two trad. The lines are steep, mostly bolted, with a couple of crack routes mixed in. Nearly every route falls in the 5.10 range, with a single easier trad line in the 5.8 range, so it suits climbers already comfortable on 5.10. The wall sits a short distance south of the Tall Wall, reached by following a wash and picking a way through boulders to its base.

ca_macondo_cliff.blurb: Macondo Cliff sits high on a ridge above the Far Side on Mount St. Helena, in the wine country north of the Bay Area. It has nine routes, six sport and three trad, from 5.7 up to 5.11b, with five of them at 5.10 and two at 5.11. The cliff is a long way from the road: the hike includes a steep third-class gully followed by a switchbacking trail, and it takes over an hour. Some of the rock is loose, so helmets and care are worthwhile, and parts of this mountain were burned in the 2017 fires.

ca_mother_boulder.blurb: Mother Boulder is the tallest boulder in the Nut Tree Boulders near Vacaville, set on the crest of the highest hill in the Hillcrest section, hidden behind a large oak. Because it is the farthest point from the road, it sees fewer visitors than the boulders lower down. It has nine problems, all bouldering, running from V0 to V5. Three are V0, two are V1, two are V3 and two are V5, so there is something for a range of abilities.

ca_trapezoid_peak.blurb: Trapezoid Peak is a steep High Sierra wall just west of Mt. Goode, seen from the Bishop Pass Trail out of South Lake. It holds nine routes, seven alpine and two trad, usually multi-pitch. They range from fourth-class and easy fifth-class ridge terrain up through the 5.10s to a cluster of hard 5.12 lines and one 5.13. The main face points east, so it gets sun early and falls into shade in the afternoon. Expect a long hike with talus at the end, and rockfall near the base of some lines.

ca_cube_the_3.blurb: The Cube is a roadside boulder near Lake Siskiyou outside Mount Shasta, beside the South Fork crag. It has nine bouldering problems, mostly between V0 and V3 with a few harder ones up to V6. Because it sits right next to where cars stop, there is almost no walk, which makes it a handy place to warm up before heading to the wall, or a short stop on its own.

ca_the_eyrie.blurb: The Eyrie is a recently developed sport crag on the ridge above The Benches, directly over The Fortress, in the Emeralds near the Yuba River. It has nine bolted routes on a wall just shy of vertical with well-featured stone. Grades run from 5.6 to the 5.10 range, with the biggest group at 5.7, and the bolting is set up with newer and moderate leaders in mind. Anchors can be reached from the top of the cliff, which makes setting up a top rope simple.
